title: Outbox
description: One outbox entry: an authorised side effect waiting to run exactly once (PRD 8.5, FR-AGT-11, FR-CHN-13, SEC-03). The harness writes it and tilo-connectors runs it; connector side-effect methods are callable only from the outbox. An entry exists only once the policy engine has authorised it (a person at a gate, or a policy below T3), so authz is always set, equal to the authz of the approval.resolved that answered approve on its gate or of the policy.applied that opened it, never of approval.requested, and the data.transfer it emits carries the same authz (OB-01, HR-7); a proposed side effect waiting at a gate is not in the outbox yet (approval.requested reserves its id). The entry names everything the connector needs: recipients, attachments, the pinned item and the destination. Rules OB-01 to OB-05 are in contracts/outbox.rules.md.

idempotency_key.description: Stable per step: a retry reuses it, and the connector runs a key at most once (OB-03).

recipients.description: Everyone the side effect reaches; equals the recipients the gate card showed (card rule CR-12).

item.description: The draft or file this entry sends, saves or shares, pinned to the version the policy engine assessed and the gate card showed; the connector sends exactly this version (OB-05). null only when the action moves no content, such as a delete.

destination.description: The thread a reply goes into or the folder a file is saved in, as the gate card showed it (OB-05); null when there is none, such as a new email.

modifiers.description: The PRD 10.4 conditions that apply to this side effect; any one makes it T3.

undo_window_s.description: Seconds the person can still cancel (PRD 10.4: L2 default 60); 0 when none.

scheduled_at.description: Earliest send time: created_at plus undo_window_s (OB-02).

state.description: queued (ready, no undo window), scheduled (waiting out its undo window), sending, sent, cancelled (undone before sending) or failed.

if.description: OB-04 (PRD 10.4): T3 always needs a person, so a policy never authorises it; any modifier makes the side effect T3, and an attachment is itself a modifier (PRD 11.4), so it is listed.
